title: Get them off the beach
notes: Opens on 1 s of black, then the Capra animated map fades up (FILM-43+FADE) under 'Dunkirk… nineteen forty'. No '1940 · DUNKIRK' card: the map says DUNKIRK top left.

The shot log's shots are 1–3 s long (Capra cuts fast), so most lines are two or three cuts. The shot log missed two cuts: shot 2 (the map) dissolves into the DUNKERQUE road sign at ≈231.4, and shot 5 cuts at ≈240.8 from dive-bombing to a line of ships on the horizon; src_max values there were set by eye from grab strips.

Plan in-points (≈03:40, 04:04, 04:52, 05:00, 05:08–05:20) were re-pinned against the picture-only file: map 218.0; destroyers line astern #7 246.6; small vessel packed with troops #33 293.8; British troops faces to camera #38 302.3; disembarking #46 317.49.

'Exhausted soldier in profile' (plan 04:12) is not at that time in this file; the nearest is #30 (≈286.5, soldiers huddled in a boat, one in profile), used under '…and an extraordinary rescue'. 'A defeat' gets two 1 s cuts of abandoned vehicles (#40 street, #41 beach).

SCENE 14 RETURN: the disembarking shot is #46, British troops walking off the quay giving thumbs-up, in-point 317.49, shot 317.29–319.65 (2.36 s, src_max 319.55). #44 (313.23, soldiers in French helmets embraced on a station platform) is its companion.
Avoid #25 (272.3–277.3: soldiers running through smoke, machine-gunners behind a cart) and #26 (burning beach aerial): they look staged/reconstructed. Avoid #47 onward (Churchill, then Pétain).

P1.07 'This is about what came after' ends on ships at sea heading away (shot 5b, #6), XD into scene 02; the plan's 'last frame of 05:20 held' would be a freeze of #46, which the cut list cannot express; do it in Premiere if preferred.
No credit string is recorded for gov.fdr.25.4 (CC0, FDR Library via archive.org); add one to the end credits if Kai wants it.
